AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Digging up all the plants
   B. Leaving the ground bare
   C. Burning the soil
   D. Covering the ground with mulch or grass

2. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. To make the compost sweeter
   B. To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   C. To keep your hands cold
   D. So the heap grows faster

3. Which of these is a brown material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh cow dung
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Fresh weeds

4. About how high should a compost heap be built? (1 mark)
   A. As flat as the ground
   B. Only one hand high
   C. As high as a house
   D. About as high as your chest

5. Why does a higher container give a faster drip? (1 mark)
   A. It is nearer the sun
   B. Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   C. It has more air
   D. It has a lid

6. What might happen if the water for a drip system is dirty? (1 mark)
   A. The plants will grow faster
   B. The water will taste better
   C. The holes may block
   D. The bucket will be lighter

7. How can you tell that a plant has enough water? (1 mark)
   A. The pot is empty
   B. The soil is dust
   C. The leaves are gone
   D. The soil is damp about a finger deep

8. Which of these is a way of collecting water for the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the roof
   B. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   C. Cutting down trees
   D. Digging up rivers

9. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Turn the flame down or move wood back
   B. Add more wood
   C. Add paraffin
   D. Open the pot and blow on it

10. Which of these can be used to keep boiled water hot? (1 mark)
   A. A hot stone
   B. A metal spoon
   C. An open basin
   D. A thermos flask

11. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Pour paraffin on it
   B. Put it out
   C. Leave it burning
   D. Add more wood

12. Why is dry firewood better than wet firewood? (1 mark)
   A. It puts out fires
   B. It burns better with less smoke
   C. It is heavier
   D. It cannot burn

13. What should the scarecrow pole be like? (1 mark)
   A. Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   B. Loose so it can fall over
   C. Very short
   D. Made of glass

14. What word means living peacefully together with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Trapping
   B. Hunting
   C. Poaching
   D. Coexisting

15. What might a hungry hare eat in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Metal
   C. Young shoots of vegetables
   D. Stones

16. What is a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A wild bird
   B. A farm tool for digging
   C. A kind of fence
   D. A figure made to look like a person to scare animals

17. What is a drill in sowing? (1 mark)
   A. A type of seed
   B. A weed
   C. A power tool
   D. A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown

18. What is a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   C. A bed for sleeping
   D. A tool for digging

19. Why is dry grass laid lightly over a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. It makes seeds fly
   B. It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   C. It makes the soil hard
   D. It stops seeds growing

20. When should the grass mulch be removed? (1 mark)
   A. When seedlings begin to appear
   B. Never
   C. After harvesting
   D. At sowing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain four benefits of conserving fuel. (4 marks)

22. Describe how to make a bottle drip for one plant. (3 marks)

23. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)

24. Give two advantages of direct sowing. (2 marks)

25. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

26. State two safety rules when making a scarecrow. (2 marks)

27. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

28. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

29. Explain why a scarecrow becomes less useful if it is never moved. (3 marks)

30. Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

2. B — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

3. B — Dry leaves
   Brown materials are dry, like dry leaves, dry grass and straw.

4. D — About as high as your chest
   A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

5. B — Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   A higher container gives a bigger push for water flowing down.

6. C — The holes may block
   Dirt gets stuck in tiny holes.

7. D — The soil is damp about a finger deep
   Feeling the soil shows if the roots have water.

8. B — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Rainwater tanks store water for dry days.

9. A — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

10. D — A thermos flask
   A flask keeps water hot so it need not be boiled again.

11. B — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

12. B — It burns better with less smoke
   Dry wood gives more heat and less smoke.

13. A — Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   A loose pole falls in the wind.

14. D — Coexisting
   To coexist is to live together.

15. C — Young shoots of vegetables
   Hares nibble young plants.

16. D — A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

17. D — A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   A drill is a shallow furrow made with a stick.

18. B — The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

19. B — It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   Mulch protects the surface.

20. A — When seedlings begin to appear
   Seedlings need light.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make tiny holes in the cap, fill the bottle with clean water, bury the neck upside down near the plant, press soil around it and refill when empty.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holes in cap, 1 mark for placing near plant, 1 mark for filling and refilling.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Roots are not disturbed, no nursery is needed, saves time and work (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds and animals soon notice it never moves, learn that it is harmless, and come back to eat the crops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for noticing, 1 mark for learning it is harmless, 1 mark for returning to the crops.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.
